requirement:
When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration
MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
The subject, `requirements.examples.authoring_inputs`, has one obligation. When evidence is authored for a named example, the example's complete fenced declaration MUST be in the mandatory input set.

The test `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It covers the obligation as follows:
- It defines an example `case` in the project markdown, with the body "Ready example. {cite}`requirements.ready` {test}`requirements.ready`".
- It calls `AssessmentSources::prepare(root.path(), "requirements.case")`, so the example is the assessment subject.
- It asserts that `subject_kind` is `AssessmentKind::Definition(DefinitionKind::Example, false)`. This confirms the subject was handled as an example.
- It asserts that the first mandatory input has `requirements == "requirements.case"`.
- It asserts that the first mandatory input's `text` equals the exact complete declaration. That is the opening fence `:::{example} case`, the body line, and the closing `:::`. The assertion is an exact `json!` array comparison, so a truncated declaration, one missing a fence line, or one with the wrong body would fail.

The same test also checks the surrounding `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` behavior. It checks deduplication through the definition count and the omission of earlier `evidence/` inputs. That behavior is cited context, so I did not reassess it.

The requirement names no further input classes or failure cases. The example in the test has no option lines, but the text does not distinguish such declarations. I therefore found no untested obligation and no inadequate assertion.
